skill.name: context-degradation
skill.description: Recognize, diagnose, and mitigate patterns of context degradation in agent systems. Use when context grows large, agent performance degrades unexpectedly, or debugging agent failures.
skill.summary: Diagnose long-context failure patterns and choose practical mitigation tactics for agent systems.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

content.value_statement: Long agent sessions can hide important context and reduce answer quality. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code detect degradation patterns and choose mitigation tactics.
actual_capabilities: Explains lost-in-middle, poisoning, distraction, confusion, and clash patterns.
Provides activation criteria for debugging long agent conversations.
Offers mitigation strategies such as compaction, filtering, isolation, and task segmentation.
Shows context layouts that place critical information at attention-favored positions.
Includes Python utilities for simulated context health analysis.
limitations: The Python attention functions use simulations, not real model internals.
Model threshold claims should be verified against current provider documentation.
The skill does not automate remediation inside external agent systems.
Detection guidance depends on user-provided context quality and task details.

use_cases.title: Agent Reliability Review
use_cases.description: Identify where long contexts reduce agent accuracy and plan targeted mitigations.

use_cases.title: Long Conversation Debugging
use_cases.description: Trace declining answer quality to poisoning, distraction, confusion, or context clash.

use_cases.title: Evaluation Design
use_cases.description: Build tests that expose lost-in-middle behavior and context length thresholds.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Conversation
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a long agent session.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this conversation for context degradation. Identify the most likely pattern and explain the main evidence in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Classify Degradation Symptoms
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these symptoms, classify them as lost-in-middle, poisoning, distraction, confusion, or clash. Include a short confidence rating for each.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Context Mitigation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a production workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a mitigation plan for this agent workflow. Include what to write, select, compress, and isolate before the next run.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Long-Context Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this long-context architecture for degradation risk. Prioritize failure modes, test coverage, operational triggers, and rollback steps.

output_examples.input: An agent forgets a requirement from the middle of a long planning session.
output_examples.output: Likely lost-in-middle. Move the requirement to the task header or final checklist, then retest the same prompt.

output_examples.input: A support agent keeps repeating an early incorrect account status after later correction.
output_examples.output: Likely context poisoning. Remove the incorrect status, restart from verified facts, and mark the correction explicitly.

output_examples.input: A research agent mixes two valid but incompatible source versions.
output_examples.output: Likely context clash. Add source priority rules and filter outdated references before loading context.

best_practices: Place critical instructions at the beginning or end of long contexts.
Filter retrieved material before adding it to active context.
Test agent behavior at increasing context sizes before production use.
anti_patterns: Do not assume larger context windows always improve reliability.
Do not preserve unverified summaries after a hallucination appears.
Do not mix unrelated tasks in one agent context without clear boundaries.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps diagnose why agent quality drops when conversations or documents become long.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. The main skill is documentation, with optional local Python analysis utilities.

faq.question: Can it prove that a model ignored context?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured evidence and likely explanations, not definitive proof of internal attention.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when long sessions produce omissions, contradictions, repeated errors, or irrelevant responses.

faq.question: How should teams apply the advice?
faq.answer: Start with context filtering, explicit priority rules, compaction triggers, and isolated task contexts.
